title: Password Reset Poisoning via Host Header

technique.summary: Poison the Host header in a password reset request so that the reset link emailed to the victim contains an attacker-controlled domain. When the victim clicks the link, their reset token is sent to the attacker.
steps: Submit a password reset request with the victim's email
Intercept the request and modify the Host header to an attacker-controlled domain
If Host header is rejected, try X-Forwarded-Host, X-Original-URL, or Forwarded headers
Check if the reset email contains a link with the attacker's domain
Set up a server to capture the incoming reset token
Use the captured token to reset the victim's password

payloads.notes: Forwarded host header — often trusted by frameworks
Dual header — Host is correct but X-Forwarded-Host overrides

bypassTechniques: Use X-Forwarded-Host, X-Host, X-Original-URL if Host is validated
Absolute URL in request line: GET https://evil.com/reset HTTP/1.1
Dangling markup injection in the email if HTML email is used
